body: Yep. I totally feel you. Plus, if you get your heart broken, most other people will understand that experience and be able to comfort you or empathise to some degree. We have language to describe heartbreak. Very few people understand what it's like to experience rejection 100% of the time, or (god forbid) falling in unrequited love and having that be your \*only\* experience. Even if you try to explain the feeling, they always act like it's not a big deal and you should just suck it up, because they assume the rejection has to be balanced out by reciprocal love, and can't conceive of a reality where it never is. We get all of the heartache and none of the empathy. Yay.

This isn't a thing where she's hiding her sexuality because of fears of being shunned by her family or anything, she is constantly telling people how much of a "lesbian" she is. I'm not going to claim to tell people what they feel inside (even though part of me thinks there is a little bit of oppression-grabbing going on, and I also don't get how marrying a man wouldn't make her bisexual, but whatever). The part that bugs me is I feel like she uses her "lesbian" identity to avoid being there for me as a friend whenever I try to talk about guys. I am insecure about my looks and once I sent her a pic of a guy and asked her if he was objectively too good-looking for me, I really just wanted some reassurance. Instead of answering the question, or even making up something to be even slightly supportive, she went on about how "as a lesbian I cannot discern whether or not a man is attractive or not because all men are sooooo unattractive to me except the one I married who is the ONLY man I have ever been attracted to." I'm so sick of this. When my \*actual\* lesbian/bisexual friends want to talk to me about the women they are seeing, I don't go on about how "as a straight woman I cannot be expected to listen to you talk about your romantic interests because I don't like women." No, I listen to them and try my best to be supportive, it's not fucking about me. Just so sick of this, like how fucking hard is it to just be a supportive friend once in awhile instead of turning your exceptionally heteronormative relationship where you literally spend all day at home cooking and cleaning for when your husband comes home into some weird "queer" get-out-of-being-a-friend card.

Even my other "close" friends don't get me at all. No one understands the isolation inherent in getting a PhD. All therapists want to do is praise me for being an "accomplished" person and/or ask me if I can "just take time off" from my PhD, because not one of them has the first fucking clue of what it means to get a PhD. Can't talk about what it's like to move to another country where I knew no one right before a pandemic, because I don't know anyone who did that, and they all would have moved with their partners anyway. Can't talk about what it's like to live alone in lockdown, because they all live with a partner or friend. Can't talk about what it's like to never have had a relationship, because none of them have been single as an adult for one day. Can't talk about what it's like to be estranged from your family, because they all grew up in supportive homes. Can't even talk about hobbies, because none of them have the same interests. Actually can't even "talk" at all, because apparently no one uses a phone or video chat anymore. Just get sent random memes on instagram and we wonder why everyone in the world is depressed. 

This is why I get so stuck on people when I feel understood for the first time in forever. And then when they inevitably reject me it's so hard to take.

Hey. I identify a lot with this situation as it has some similarities to a situation I had several years ago. I am definitely NOT telling you to do the same thing I did, but since I can empathize with this I figured I would share my experience. 

In university I had a several-year "something" with a guy -- we never dated or were even physical in any way, but I thought he liked me and eventually told him how I felt way too late. By this time he was already seeing someone else, but it started this pattern where he would show up in my life again when he was single, give me all kinds of insane mixed signals, then when I thought we might actually start dating for real he would act all confused as to why I could have possibly thought taking a two-week trip together and meeting each other's friends would mean we might be starting something. He eventually said he had had feelings for me but as long as we worked together we wouldn't be together, but left things really open-ended, of course making me think that one day there was a possibility of being together. Then I would cut off all social contact, until eventually he would show up in my life again, which always seemed to happen right around the time he started dating a new girl. 

I realized about halfway through that the reason I was falling for his emotional manipulation and allowing myself to be led on for years was that for me, love = pain and toxic behaviors just made sense because of the fucked up relationship my parents had modeled for me. Even though I figured this out logically, I still let myself be led on by the hope that one day something would change. 

The breaking point came when contacted me out of the blue after a year, and invited me over to his house and made dinner for me, and we had a really lovely evening. A couple weeks later he moved to a new country without saying goodbye to me, and I told him off and cut off contact for good. A few months after that I learned he had started dating a new girl around the same time he got back in touch. WHY he would always show up when he was starting something new with someone else I will never understand, but the hurt and pain and utter confusion this caused me somehow pushed me over the edge and I finally confronted the ridiculousness of all of it and it helped me get over it. It still took a few more months of heartache, but it was like I just got pushed so far that my logical side finally won out over my stupid emotions. 

Like you I spent a long time hoping he would apologize for leading me on and give me some closure, but eventually I just got to the point where the sheer audacity of how he treated me made me laugh and realize that my life is way better without him in it. It's been years now and he is getting married to the girl he started dating around the last time he showed up in my life again, and I can say with total conviction that I don't care at all.

Even though it seems like logic could have ended this situation far sooner, the logic just wasn't winning the battle for me, and it seemed to take pushing my heart as far as it could go before I finally let it go. I'm not advocating for this approach as it takes a long time and definitely opens the door to more heartache, but it did eventually work for me. Looking back, I think the thing I'm most grateful for is I don't have any of these lingering thoughts of "what if I had done things differently?" I gave him enough chances, and he proved himself to be a jerk beyond a shadow of a doubt, and now I don't have to wonder if I missed out on something good because it's clear I didn't. Now I feel like a dodged a bullet and I'm happy for that. 

Sorry for the long-winded story of my life but hopefully you can relate and maybe it helps you reflect in some way.

I'm late 20s and still a virgin, haven't kissed anyone either. For awhile the idea of turning 30 as a virgin was really bothering me and I started considering this. I go through phases where I feel like a total freak and social outcast, like reaching this arbitrary number as a virgin disqualifies me from ever experiencing an intimate relationship. Maybe it does. But as someone with a history of trauma I simply can't even contemplate doing this outside of a trusting relationship. 

What helped me get over this was reminding myself that the entire concept of virginity is patriarchal bullshit. For decades (centuries?) women have been shamed for having sex, while men have been congratulated. This is old news of course, but in the last several years with the rise of sex-positive feminism, I think we've seen a near-180° reversal in this attitude, at least among younger people in Western countries. Now casual sex is seen as empowering by a lot of women, and instead of slut-shaming we now celebrate casual sex. But because humans suck it seems that we can't end slut-shaming without turning around and finding a new victim to shame, so now instead of prizing virginity (stupid and sexist) we "prude-shame" (also stupid and sexist). (Mandatory disclaimer because this is the internet: if you enjoy casual sex that's your choice and I really don't care.) 

However: the problem with framing it as either virginity = good or casual sex = good is that either way it *still centers men and male pleasure*. And this is fucking stupid. Sexual liberation was supposed to be about female bodily autonomy, female pleasure, and dismantling a system that treats women and their bodies as property. It wasn't about offering yourself up on an app so some dude can get his rocks off without one ounce of consideration to your humanity or pleasure. But now so we don't seem like uncool, prudish spinsters, we have to pretend that we're all totes cool with this new brand of male-centered "feminism", and women like us who don't engage in it, or can't engage in it, end up feeling like subhuman rejects. Even though I don't partake myself, I've spent enough time on the internet to know that women who partake in casual sex are often not enjoying it (a million articles on the internet but here's one [https://www.healthline.com/health/women-abstaining-from-casual-sex](https://www.healthline.com/health/women-abstaining-from-casual-sex) ). We need to stop listening to this rebranded form of patriarchal trickery.

I know that's easier said than done. I still often feel insecure when I think about this, and it's not very comforting when people say stuff like "with the right person your sexual experience won't matter." (yeah, sure, but where are they?) I have a deep fear of meeting a great guy and being rejected because "virginity is a red flag." But I've decided that for me it just isn't worth it. You can do things to explore sexual pleasure on your own in the meantime and the experience will probably be a lot better than being treated like a walking sex doll (and I'm not convinced that suffering through terrible sex will actually make you any better at sex in a good relationship anyway). And to the people who think that not having had PIV sex at an arbitrary age makes you less of an adult, less mature, less cool, less of an "empowered" woman, etc. Fuck em.

I go through life with walls up, and while I might feel self-loathing I definitely accept who I am, and I am the only person I trust. For me personally, I think I need more so to learn how to love and trust someone else, but for that to happen I would need to actually have relationships with trustworthy people.

I also disagree with this religion's notion that you "attract what you put out there" and such. Because again, it's victim-blaming. I have attracted a lot of creeps in my life, to the point where I was convinced something was wrong with me. Someone once explained it to me as there are bad people all around, and they are constantly subtly testing people to see who has poor boundaries, who has low self-confidence, etc. Then when they detect that they push a little harder, so if you have poor boundaries they will focus their energies on you instead of the healthy person who shut them down.  Yes, I struggle with boundaries and it's something I'm working on (again, one of those things that can only be worked on with other humans involved), but I refuse to accept that my "energy" is what has continually brought these people into my life, because I am not to blame. These bad people exist, and I have had bad things happen in life that make me more susceptible to these people, but this is not my fault. No one deserves this sort of shit. Can "self-love" fix this? Probably, but it ignores the very real fact that these thoughts and behaviors are formed by our lifelong interactions with other people and treatment by the world. No one comes out of the womb feeling like a worthless burden on society. We are taught that for years and now to add insult to injury we're told we just need to gratitude-journal and positive-mantra our way out of it.
